answer: Sybil farms thrive when a new identity is cheaper than the vote it buys. Require each applicant to lock a timber stake that cannot be withdrawn until it has stood through a tundra of several quiet epochs with no colliding device, host, or key-graph fingerprints. Sponsorship is scarce: only a pearl of established neighbors, chosen by a hash of the applicant's public key and the epoch seed—not by the applicant—may countersign. If two names later collapse into one operator cluster, every still-locked stake is slashed, so cloned herds bleed capital instead of buying votes.
